html:
The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in the heart of Africa, with its capital Bangui on the Ubangi River. France ruled it as Ubangi-Shari from 1903 until independence in 1960.

As part of French Equatorial Africa, it was handed to private concession companies that forced people to gather rubber, with great cruelty. The Kongo-Wara revolt of 1928 to 1931 rose against forced labour.

  • 1958: Barthélemy Boganda, the leader of the independence movement, named the country; he died in a plane crash in 1959.
  • 1960: independence.
  • 1966: Jean-Bédel Bokassa seized power. In 1977 he crowned himself emperor of the Central African Empire.
  • 1979: French troops removed him.
  • 2013: rebels took Bangui, starting a civil war between mostly Muslim and mostly Christian militias.

France has intervened with troops many times since independence.
sum: The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in the heart of Africa, with its capital Bangui on the Ubangi River. France ruled it as Ubangi-Shari from 1903 until independence in 1960.
